title: PHA 104 - Pharmaceutical Chemistry and Dispensing Practice

items.q: Which of the following best describes Chemical incompatibility?
o: an insoluble calcium salt used as an antacid and as a mild source of calcium
a reaction between ingredients that alters the identity of one of them
a person licensed to sell only a limited range of packaged medicines
a visible change such as separation, precipitation or colour change on mixing
items.s: Chemical incompatibility: a reaction between ingredients that alters the identity of one of them. The other options describe Physical incompatibility, Patent medicine vendor, Calcium carbonate.

items.q: Which statement correctly defines Solvent?
o: the liquid in which a substance is dissolved to form a solution
a visible change such as separation, precipitation or colour change on mixing
a solution that holds as much dissolved solid as it can at that temperature
an unwanted change when two ingredients are mixed in one preparation
items.s: Solvent: the liquid in which a substance is dissolved to form a solution. The other options describe Saturated solution, Physical incompatibility, Incompatibility.

items.q: Sterile product may be defined as
o: the agreement reached between patient and prescriber about how treatment is used
an added agent that prevents microbes from multiplying in a multi-dose product
a preparation free from all viable microbes, made for injection or for the eye
the breakdown of a substance by reaction with water
items.s: Sterile product: a preparation free from all viable microbes, made for injection or for the eye. The other options describe Antimicrobial preservative, Concordance, Hydrolysis.

items.s: Good manufacturing practice: the set of rules that ensures products are made to consistent quality. The other options describe Dry heat sterilisation, Antimicrobial preservative, Hydrolysis.
